utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone, and good morning to you, Madam Registrar. If you could kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Merci. All the accused are here. I don't want to make the same mistake as yesterday. Mr. McCloskey is on his own. And, from the Defence teams, I notice the absence of Mr. Ostojic. I think that's it. Okay. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I would just like to present Mr. Stojanovic who is joining the Defence team for these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Lazarevic and welcome, sir. Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. One of the first exhibits this morning will be the duty officer work book that everyone is familiar with. In discussions with the Defence, I've been trying to find a best way to go through. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry. I see those curtains down, and I think we are closed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. It's one further case of not looking, never looking behind, Mr. McCloskey. So let's redact this and let's go into closed session straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. President, and Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I initially asked for some additional time to respond to some issues that were raised in our friend's response on the issue of General Smith's expert statement. I didn't want to engage in surreplies or extended oral argument, neither is it something that we wanted to take the Court's time up with. And as time has passed and in consultation with my friends, most of the issues I had wanted to raise have resolved themselves. There are two that remain, and I think that we can dispose of them or raise them pretty quickly. The first is there is a case to which I'd like to bring the Court's attention that neither party cited in our filings. And where I come from, if you miss a case or if you see a case later on, whether it hurts you or especially if it hurts you, you have an obligation to bring it to the Court's attention. This is a case that, I think, that cuts both ways, and I just wanted to advise the Court of its existence. It is the 16 November 2006 Milutinovic decision on the Ojdanic motion to preclude parties from calling expert witnesses. For the most part, the substance of what is in this decision, and it's discussed briefly in a couple of foot notes, has been address, but it's a decision that's out there and I just wanted to bring it to the Court's attention. That's the first issue, Your Honours. The second is the degree of overlap, if any, between the expert reports of Mr. Butler and the expert statement of General Smith, and I think we both left our arguments rather vague in that respect. I suspect that it's because, I can speak for myself only, that we presumed that the Court would review both reports during the course of its deliberation. Subsequent discussions, with respect to other exhibits and materials, made me think that perhaps the Court would not take that step to read both reports or all reports in coming to its decision; and if that's the case, I wanted to elaborate a little bit more on our position, that they do not overlap, that they are complementary and not redundant of each other. If the Trial Chamber does intend to read these reports, then I'll sit down, and I won't have anything further to say. I think I can leave it in the Court's hands to parse out the various sections of the reports and make that determination; otherwise, I'd like to say a few words about how, in my submission, they do not overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The reports will be read.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. I have one witness planning matter, if I could just address very briefly. I think it's important for planning purposes for everyone concerned. It's to some degree speculative, but there is enough that we have to deal with, I think, sooner than later to bring to the Court's attention, and that is with respect to the witnesses number 2 and 32. Witness 32, Thomas Dibb is scheduled to testify the 15th of October, and that is a Monday. He is travelling from Afghanistan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'll stop you there. I don't see how he can testify on that Monday, because on the 9th we continue with the cross-examination of the previous witness and he won't finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's my submission, Your Honour. That's why I wanted to bring this to the Court's attention. We would ask, and I've contacted my friends, (redacted) at least -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's redact. Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I would ask that we interrupt the testimony of the current witness so that we can put on Mr. Dibb, who I believe will be a relatively short witness. His travel has been planned long ago. He is in country in Afghanistan doing de-mining work. This was the only time period that he had available to come here to testify. Again, I don't think it would be more than a day or two maximum. I don't intend to examine him for more than an hour and a half, if that. So we would ask that we be able to put him on the stand and get him off the stand in a day or two and then resume the cross-examination of this witness so that we can accommodate and otherwise I'm afraid unavailable witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there any objection from the Defence teams? The understanding would be, so that I make it clear, that there will not be an interruption of any cross-examination halfway through. That's what I would definitely guarantee you. Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That's our position, Mr. President. That we do not feel it is appropriate to brake the cross-examination into two parts. It has to be ongoing and finish in one part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I could anticipate what you are saying that for.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer, I think we can plan accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just to make sure I understand, when we speak of breaking, we are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. There is --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think this is something that both sides may need to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the problem. I see Mr. Josse, Mr. Zivanovic, Mr. Bourgon, and now Mr. Haynes engaged in a --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: On that, Your Honour, I suspect, with all due respect to him, Your Honour may have misunderstood Mr. Bourgon's submission, and I think that's what we were all telling him. So I think he may need to address the Chamber again. That's all I have to say on this issue. I would quite like to return briefly to the General Smith issue when I get a chance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, our position, and I think I speak for all, everyone on the Defence side, there should be no interruption whatsoever during cross-examination of the complete cross-examination by the seven co-accused in this case, from start to finish. So, therefore, we do not consent and we object to the request of Mr. Thayer, asking for a break of one, two, or three days. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I misunderstood you. I apologise for that. I thought no interruption during any particular cross-examination. So you do have an objection, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I mean, this witness may be otherwise unavailable. I don't have any objection to not interrupting a particular cross. So if my friends can somehow plan accordingly during that 9th, 10th and 11th period, if there is somebody with three days of cross, then I think that is a fair resolution to this logistical issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just add, we are most willing to accommodate the Prosecution with any scheduling of witnesses so. Our position has nothing no do with the witness who has to come, and we can play and negotiate anything with my colleague to make sure that he can come at another time. Our concerns are strictly related to this witness for whom we want to do a unique cross-examination in a row without any interruption. I believe, Mr. President, that it is important not only for us, but also even for the witness himself. The Trial Chamber has given him --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of October, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.02 p.m.,
